beliefs.practice: Read the Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or a config file referenced by .env, fail fast on startup with a clear error if missing or invalid, and never commit the real secret to source control.

Create a single shared MongoDB client (PyMongo / Motor) at FastAPI application startup (using the lifespan event) and reuse that connection pool for all requests instead of creating a client per request.

Configure the MongoDB driver with sensible connection options: TLS enabled (tls=true), a short serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g., 5000 ms), and a bounded connection pool (maxPoolSize set to a reasonable value for the app, e.g., 50), to avoid resource exhaustion and long hangs.

Do not store raw credentials in code; use environment variables or Azure Key Vault for the connection string and other secrets; provide a .env.example that contains only placeholders (no real secrets).

On startup, perform a simple connectivity check (e.g., a findOne or ping against the sample_retail_03 database) and surface any authentication/permission errors as actionable messages so the operator fixes credentials/config early.

Use a dedicated database name (sample_retail_03) as required, and create/verify the required collections and indexes at app bootstrap or in a separate provisioning script rather than implicitly relying on lazy creation during requests.

Choose and declare an explicit partition/shard key for the products collection (e.g., category or product_id prefix) at creation time to avoid hot partitions and to support scale; ensure the app always includes the partition key in queries that should be targeted.

Model product documents to include a canonical product_id (indexed/unique), an embeddings field with fixed-length numeric array (float32), and compact textual attributes used for filtering; enforce an embedding dimensionality and type at ingest time.

During bulk ingestion of 10,000 product transactions, use batching and the bulkWrite API (or driver bulk inserts) with sizes like 500–2000 documents per batch instead of inserting one document at a time, to reduce latency and RU consumption.

For vector fields, create a vector index configured with the correct dimensionality and similarity metric (cosine) and tune the ANN algorithm parameters (e.g., algorithm=hnsw, M and efConstruction / efSearch or equivalent) appropriate to the index implementation to balance recall and query cost.

If the platform does not support native cosine similarity on vectors, store normalized unit vectors (L2-normalized) and use inner-product (dot product) search on those normalized vectors to emulate cosine similarity reliably.

Keep the vector field excluded from default (B-tree) indexes and only index it via the platform's dedicated vector index mechanism; also exclude large text blobs from general indexing to reduce RU costs.

Create additional conventional indexes used by the app: ensure product_id is indexed (unique or primary lookup), and add compound indexes for common filters (e.g., category + brand) to avoid collection scans during substitute candidate filtering.

Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient errors, and specifically detect and handle rate-limiting responses (HTTP 429 / RequestRateTooLarge) by honoring platform-provided retry-after headers (e.g., x-ms-retry-after-ms) before retrying.

Monitor RU/throughput consumption and provision or enable autoscale appropriately for ingestion and production workloads; bulk ingestion should be rate-limited to avoid sustained 429s and unnecessary RU charge spikes.

When returning the top-K substitutes, limit how much document data is read from disk: projection the response to only fields needed by the UI (product_id, title, price, thumbnail) and avoid returning the full embedding vector unless necessary.

Implement server-side or driver-side paging for any candidate filtering step (avoid reading entire collection into memory) and apply filtered vector search (candidate pre-filter by category/brand) before KNN to reduce compute and RU costs.

Validate and sanitize any input product IDs or query parameters to avoid injection-style attacks on queries, and use typed ODM validation (Beanie/Pydantic) for incoming data shapes to fail early and clearly.
Use float32 arrays for embeddings (not strings) to reduce storage and RAM footprint, and persist embeddings in a consistent endianness and dtype expected by the vector index implementation.

Instrument the application with basic telemetry (latency, error counts, RU consumption per operation, vector search recall/latency) and include health endpoints; log helpful operational context but never log secrets or full vector values.
